note:
Class 6B, week of 16 November. Notes for myself.

Aarav Sharma has missed four days this month. His mother Sunita told me on the phone (98765 43210) that his father lost his job at the mill and the family cannot pay for anything extra this term; Aarav now helps at the family tea stall before school. He is bright in maths but has not handed in homework for two weeks.

Meenal reads well aloud but freezes in written tests. She needs extra writing practice, and the remedial writing club meets after the last bell. She told me she has epilepsy and is afraid of having a seizure in the exam hall. Her roll no. 6B/23. She walks six kilometres home to Rampur Kalan and has to leave school at the last bell to reach home before dark.

Kabir and Ishaan fight most days during group work. Kabir's parents are separating and he is staying with his grandmother. Ishaan finishes early and gets bored.

Tanvi is far ahead in reading. She could help others, but she is shy. Her family does not have a smartphone or an internet connection.

Lesson
Class: Class 6
Subject: English
Topic: Writing a short description of a place
Length: 40 minutes

draft.title: Writing a short description of a place

items.heading: Starter (5 minutes)
items.text: The teacher introduces the topic of writing a short description of a place. The pupils think about a familiar place and share one descriptive word. Materials needed are the blackboard and chalk.

items.heading: Teach (10 minutes)
items.text: The teacher explains how to structure a short description using sensory details. The pupils listen and note down key adjectives on their paper. Materials needed are notebooks and pens.

items.heading: Practise (15 minutes)
items.text: The teacher guides the class to write a short paragraph describing the school courtyard. The pupils write their descriptions independently using the taught structure. Materials needed are paper and pens.

items.heading: Check (10 minutes)
items.text: The teacher invites volunteers to read their descriptions aloud to the class. The pupils listen and offer positive feedback. Materials needed are the written paragraphs.

items.heading: Homework (0 minutes)
items.text: Write a short description of your room at home in five sentences.

board: Writing a Short Description of a Place
2. Use sensory details (sight, sound, smell, touch)
Example: The courtyard is bright and noisy.
sheet: Write a short paragraph describing the school courtyard.
Introduction: Name the place and general feel.
Detail 3: What can you smell or touch?
Conclusion: A final sentence about how it makes you feel.

Listen to your partner's description and help them improve it.

ticket.question: What type of details should you include when describing a place?
Why do we use adjectives in a description?
ticket.answer: To describe nouns and make the writing more vivid

ticket.question: What place are we describing today?
